solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Car, note, missing second motorway

indicators.note: missing second says the word loses its second instance of the letter named, not the first

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A car journey narrated as a list: a note left behind, and a second motorway skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: MINIM has two Ms; 'second' tells you to drop the later one, leaving MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a small British automobile model, famous since the 1960s.

clue.text: Soft, or daft, in a way

indicators.note: daft means silly or crazy, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a person is soft, or perhaps daft, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal hedge meaning somewhat or to some extent.

clue.text: One old-fashioned hero

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters are reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: A nostalgic description of a hero from the old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' looks like a single adjective, but the hyphen hides a split into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired and worshipped, much as a hero is looked up to.

clue.text: State north of Washington and New York

definitions.text: State north of Washington and New York

parts.words: State north of Washington and New York
parts.note: state here means a nation, and the country in question borders both Washington State and New York State to the north

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like another US state, but it means a sovereign country; Washington and New York are both US states on the northern border.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American nation lies directly along the northern frontier of both those American states.

clue.text: Take part in protest and offer inconclusive outcome

indicators.note: Take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to join a demonstration and make a proposal, ending without a resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a deadlock where neither side wins, an outcome that settles nothing.

clue.text: I'm forced to open up about boy punished for crime

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: pried means levered open, forced to open
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they are being made to come clean about a lad who was punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jailed is a common penalty for criminal offences, so jailed people were punished.

clue.text: Reacted aggressively in end of letter the writer sent

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who refers to themselves as I
posted means sent by mail

explanation.surface: Someone responded angrily within the closing lines of a letter they mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To riposte is to make a quick, sharp retort, a counterattack in words or in fencing.

clue.text: Audible cast, from beginning to end

indicators.note: Audible says the word is as heard when spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: threw means cast, past tense of throw

explanation.surface: A description of an audiobook's performers heard right the way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean completely, all the way, as in reading a book through.

clue.text: Fall in midst of ruin, mutually overturned

indicators.note: overturned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in midst of says the letters sit in the middle of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A collapse amid shared ruin, everything turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fall in midst' as the definition, but 'in midst of' is the signal that the letters are tucked inside 'ruin, mutually'; the definition is just 'Fall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Wife put in grave situation when Richard was discontented?

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to put in a grave

explanation.surface: A wife is buried in a sombre period when Richard was unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III opens: 'Now is the winter of our discontent', spoken by Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: The cold season is the time Shakespeare's Richard named in his famous opening line about discontent.

clue.text: Those who make money on line as students

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the earners come after the line letter

parts.note: earners are people who make money

explanation.surface: Wage-earners working online while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners are people being taught, such as pupils on a course.

clue.text: Composition of the year, a set of concertos

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what the year is made up of, its spring, summer, autumn and winter
second meaning: Vivaldi's famous set of four violin concertos

explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' suggests a piece of music; it is first read as what makes up a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi's group of four violin concertos bears this title, and the year likewise consists of four quarters.

clue.text: Like certain plants about to be put in awfully bare house

indicators.note: put in says the short letter is placed inside the scrambled letters
awfully means badly, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A description of plants growing in a sparsely furnished house.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaceous plants have soft, non-woody stems that die back each year, like border perennials.

clue.text: Ring heartless females up in part of Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed from the word

parts.note: girls are females

explanation.surface: Phoning cold-hearted women somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Extent of coverage in article incompletely perused

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: incompletely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to peruse is to read

explanation.surface: How much ground an article covers, only partly read.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is the size or range a thing covers, such as a surface measurement.

clue.text: What's upsetting to many in a paradox

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what a contradiction could be that bothers so many people.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinomy is a contradiction between two principles that each seem reasonable, a philosophical puzzle.

clue.text: Lift taking a lot of people? I squeezed in

indicators.note: squeezed in says the single letter is pushed inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a great number, a crowd

explanation.surface: A crowded elevator, the speaker wedged among many passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising loads, such as a winch or a crane.

clue.text: Wanting a drink, son gets stuck into a lot of XXXX

indicators.note: gets stuck into says the single letter is placed inside the number word

parts.note: XXXX is forty in Roman numerals; most of it, XXX, is thirty

explanation.surface: XXXX is an Australian beer brand, so a parched son is downing plenty of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer reading is the misdirection: read XXXX as Roman numerals and take three of the four Xs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thirsty is feeling the need for liquid refreshment.

clue.text: Fellow in North

explanation.surface: A man living up in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a native of Finland is a fellow from the north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a person from Finland, a Nordic country in northern Europe.

clue.text: New arrangement for violin, to an avid composer

indicators.note: a new arrangement of a piece reorders it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh violin arrangement written for an enthusiastic composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi was a Venetian Baroque composer, famed for his violin concertos.

clue.text: So-called mother providing environment that's kind

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Mother ..., the personified natural world
second meaning: the natural world around us

explanation.surface: A caring mother figure who provides a gentle setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers the personified Mother figure, the physical world and a type or character.

clue.text: Cowed as a force goes on attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes on means sits on top of, so these letters come before the attack word

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone intimidated as an armed unit launches an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cowed is to be frightened into submission, so scared.

clue.text: Like those recently delivered from one disorderly former province

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994

explanation.surface: Something arriving from one unruly ex-province.
explanation.walkthrough: NATAL was a South African province, now part of KwaZulu-Natal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal refers to newborn babies, those just born.

clue.text: Openings for lawyer examining some testimony in case

indicators.note: openings are the starts, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A barrister scrutinising part of a witness's evidence during a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Lest is a conjunction meaning for fear that, so as to avoid.

clue.text: Bound to get out of jail

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a leap, a jump
second meaning: to free someone from prison

explanation.surface: Someone certain to escape from prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a jump and helping a prisoner escape custody.

clue.text: Contradictory responses to request for peaceful retreat

parts.note: a refusal, the reply that contradicts the yes that follows it
an agreement, a yes in answer to a request

explanation.surface: Asking for a quiet getaway and getting mixed replies.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works as a whole: two replies to a request that contradict each other, a refusal and then consent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded, sheltered corner where one can be quiet.

clue.text: Person with something to add when things get most heated?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who sums, adding figures up
second meaning: the hottest season of the year

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as 'one who sums', pronounced differently from the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The warmest season shares its spelling with someone who does addition.

clue.text: Test broadcast on TV channel for minister

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means after, so the test episode follows the channel

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
a pilot is a trial episode of a TV series

explanation.surface: A trial programme aired on a satellite station, aimed at clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV network.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is old slang for a clergyman, especially a military chaplain.
